text:
vivian: noticed a repeating tail pattern on apac-edge rack r22 starting ~01:40 UTC. p95 pulses to ~850ms in short ~20-45s bursts every few minutes. logs point to one tenant using GPUDirect RDMA transfers (tenant-rdma) + heavy checkpointing.

karim: yikes. GPUDirect can bypass normal PCIe arbitration and produce DMA bursts that saturate host PCIe root complex and NVSwitch queues. can you paste a metric snippet?

vivian: pasted short window:
```
2026-09-12T01:42:10Z rack=r22 host=apac-r22-04 gpu0 util=93 nvlink=80Gb/s pcie_tx=5.8GB/s nic_tx=0.4GB/s
2026-09-12T01:42:10Z rack=r22 host=apac-r22-04 gpu1 util=25 nvlink=9Gb/s pcie_tx=0.3GB/s nic_tx=0.02GB/s
2026-09-12T01:42:10Z rack=r22 host=apac-r22-05 gpu0 util=92 nvlink=78Gb/s pcie_tx=5.5GB/s nic_tx=0.5GB/s
```

olga: that pcie_tx bimodality screams DMA bursts. this is different from pure NVLink saturation — PCIe root complex contention can stall DMA completion and make latency-sensitive inference wait.

infra-bot: [ALERT] apac-edge/r22: p95 latency > 800ms for 10m (rule: infra.latency.p95)

karim: immediate mitigation options: (A) throttle tenant-rdma's GPUDirect transfers via runtime cap (if the runtime exposes it), (B) soft-evict their batch replicas to an iso-shed pool, (C) apply host-level eBPF PCIe bandwidth shaping (experimental), (D) schedule fabric reservation windows for their nightly batch runs. low-risk first?

vivian: prefer (B) + (D) short-term. moving heavy replicas to iso-shed should reduce collisions, and a reservation window gives predictable tail behavior during their scheduled runs. can we do a dry-run placement to see PDB impact?

olga: running dry-run: tenant-rdma has 6 batch replicas on r22, 2 respect PDB. moving 4 should be safe. command I'll run if we agree:
```
apictl placement reschedule --rack r22 --label tenant=tenant-rdma --to-pool iso-shed-apac --grace 90s
```

karim: also, add a temporary per-tenant PCIe cap if supported by our quota proxy: `apictl quota set --tenant tenant-rdma --pcie-share 0.5 --auto-revert 30m` — will dampen the worst bursts while we reschedule.

vivian: go ahead with both. olga, run the reschedule. karim, set the quota. post-reschedule we'll keep a reservation window and talk to tenant about migrating to async checkpointing.

ops-bot: user olga invoked placement reschedule (tenant=tenant-rdma) on rack r22

infra-bot: quota manager: pcie_share override accepted for tenant. user karim invoked `apictl quota set --tenant tenant-rdma --pcie-share 0.5 --auto-revert 30m`

vivian: reschedule in progress: 3/6 moved, 1 blocking on PDB, 2 in progress. p95 dropped to ~240ms after first two moves.

karim: nice. even with partial moves the bursts are lessening. will leave pcie_share override for 30m as safety.

olga: recommending follow-up items: 1) add per-tenant PCIe TX metrics to dashboard (owner: olga), 2) add an alert for PCIe asymmetry per-rack (pcie_tx.stddev > 0.25), 3) pilot a small eBPF shim to rate-limit kernel DMA submission for noisy tenants (experimental, owner: karim).

vivian: agreed. also propose adding a "fabric reservation window" feature: tenants can declare scheduled heavy windows and infra will carve an iso-shed slice for that window automatically (owner: infra product). lowers blast radius and keeps costs predictable.

karim: quick note on eBPF shim: it can help shape PCIe bursts by adding micro-delays to userland submitters, but it's invasive and needs stage testing — won't be our go-to today, but worth a spike.

infra-bot: action items logged: infra-issue-9012 (pcie metrics), infra-issue-9013 (pcie asymmetry alert), infra-spike-9014 (eBPF pcie shaping), product-ticket-1219 (fabric reservation windows).

vivian: tenant team reached back: they're open to using reservation windows and to investigating async checkpointing. I'll coordinate a short runbook for "noisy GPU tenant during heavy GPUDirect ops" and post to #incidents after 30m stable.

olga: reschedule complete; p95 steady ~190ms for last 12m. leaving temp quota and placement tag for 45m, then revert.

karim: thanks all. if this repeats we escalate to carving tenant-rdma into a small dedicated slice during their heavy windows. closing loop after the incident note is posted. :white_check_mark:
